newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk PM faces meeting with secularist military.
newsitem.headline: Turk PM faces meeting with secularist military.

text.p: Turkey's secularist generals are putting new pressure on Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan in a confrontation that has unsettled the stock market and opened cracks in the coalition government.
They come face to face on Saturday with armed forces chief Ismail Hakki Karadayi insisting that the growing, government-fostered role of Islam in the nation's life must be curbed.

Erbakan's key coalition ally, pro-Western conservative Tansu Ciller, denied a press report on Friday that she was about to pull her True Path party out of modern Turkey's first Islamist-led government.

The armed forces chief told the state-run Anatolian new agency on Friday that while the army intended to keep out of politics "There are some developments in our country against the basic constitutional properties of our republic to which our people and our armed forces are extremely sensitive.
"Nobody can remain insensible and impartial in the face of this. But the place to resolve this is parliament,".
Generals have ousted three governments since 1960 but are reluctant to stage another coup for fear of damaging NATO member Turkey's bid to get closer to Europe.
The army demanded an anti-Islamist crackdown in February but now feels the government has failed to carry it out as promised.

Military leaders are expected to confront Erbakan and his key ministers in the powerful National Security Council. The monthly meeting is scheduled to begin at 3 p.m. (1200 GMT) on Saturday and will be chaired by President Suleyman Demirel.
Talks were likely to deal with a key army demand, opposed by Erbakan's Welfare Party, that the state's secularist education be extended to eight years from five, media reports said.
The planned education reforms would marginalise religious secondary schools, the breeding ground of future Islamists.

Ciller's denial that she was quitting the 10-month-old government helped to steady a plunging Istanbul stock market on Friday. She and Erbakan held almost two hours of hastily arranged talks on Friday evening.

Two anti-Islamist ministers from Ciller's party are in open rebellion against Welfare for stalling on the military's plans to restrict religious education, penalise Islamist dress and move against Islamist business and media.
A Welfare threat to take legal action against a general who abused Erbakan in comments seen on television further exacerbated Islamist relations with the army on Thursday.
The commander called Erbakan a "pimp" for going on pilgrimage to the Moslem holy city of Mecca as the guest of conservative Saudi King Fahd.
The army is practically the only state authority in a large chunk of south-eastern Turkey where troops are fighting Kurdish separatist rebels.
